description:
FILED s470bt (Opus, 2026-09-06) by the B6 IR conformance corpus.  Each row is
its own fix and its own corpus case; they are one task only because each is a
singleton.  SPLIT when scheduled.  All probed perl 5.40.3 vs PCL main cd34df72.

(1) `\(@array, LIST)` does not distribute          [022-array]
      my @b = (7,8); my @r = \(@b, 9);
      print scalar(@r), " ", ${$r[0]}, ${$r[1]}, "\n";
    perl  3 78 ... then dies "Not a SCALAR reference" on ${$r[2]}
    PCL   2 789
    -- perl's `\` distributes over a parenthesised list AND over an array's
    ELEMENTS; PCL takes one ref to the whole array.

(2) the symbolic last-index                        [237-refs 238-refs]
      no strict 'refs'; our @ga = (1,2,3);
      print "last=", $#{'main::ga'}, "\n";
    perl  last=2      PCL  last=7

(3) utf8::is_utf8 on a byte string                 [243-regex]
      my $s = "\x{e2}\x{80}\x{99}";
      print "flag=", (utf8::is_utf8($s)?1:0), " len=", length($s), "\n";
    perl  flag=0 len=3     PCL  flag=1 len=3
    -- PCL has no downgraded representation, so the flag is always on.  Note
    the LENGTH agrees, so this is the introspection only.

(4) `eval @array`                                  [295-sprintf]
      my @a = qw(a b c d); my @b = eval @a; print "b=@b err=[$@]\n";
    perl  b=4 err=[]
    PCL   b= err=[Undefined subroutine &main::ARRAY called ...]
    -- eval's operand is an EXPR in scalar context, so `eval @a` is
    `eval("4")`.

(5) `exists $string->{k}` under `use strict refs`  [253-regex]
      use strict; my $ns = "plain"; print exists $ns->{k};
    perl  dies: Can't use string ("plain") as a HASH ref while "strict refs"
    PCL   answers '' and continues

(6) a foreach alias to a SORT of literals is read-only   [272-sort]
      for my $x (sort ("b","a")) { $x .= "!" }
    perl  dies: Modification of a read-only value attempted
    PCL   modifies happily
    (the `sort split(...)` spelling in the same case agrees -- only literals
    diverge)

(7) a trailing BAREWORD statement is emitted as a CALL    [213-oo 239-refs]
      no strict 'refs'; print "one\n";
      PERL
    perl  runs, prints one, exits 0 (a bareword is a string constant under
          `no strict subs`, and a statement whose value is discarded)
    PCL   dies: Undefined subroutine &main::PERL called
    -- #266's family ("a bare NAME is a CALL only where it is CALLABLE"); the
    STATEMENT position is the uncovered spelling.

(8) a pipe with a `:utf8` layer on one end          [258-regex]
      pipe $in2, $out2; binmode $out2, ':utf8'; binmode $in2;
      syswrite $out2, "abc\n"; my $l2 = readline $in2;
    perl  dies (exit 255) after the first half's output
    PCL   reads the line and exits 0
    -- the least understood of the eight; the layer/`syswrite` interaction was
    not narrowed further.  Sibling of #1115.


=== VERDICT PER SINGLETON (s473h, Opus, 2026-09-08) ===

The brief's seven, in the task's order.  Every one probed vs perl 5.40.3
first; probes in scratch/s473h/probe/.

(1) `\(@array, LIST)` â **SHIPPED, but NOT the bug this task describes.**
    The task's premise is STALE: measured, `\(@b, 9)` gives 2 refs
    (ARRAY, SCALAR) in BOTH perl and PCL, and perl gives 2, not 3.  What
    actually made ir-conform 022-refs fail is the NEXT expression:
    `${$r[0]}` on an ARRAY ref must die `Not a SCALAR reference`, and PCL
    read the array.  Fixed by the REFERENT rule (%p-aggregate-referent-p,
    commit e13305a8); the case's stdout now matches perl byte for byte and
    its known-fail row is re-pointed at #1247 (exit 255 vs 1), which is its
    whole residue.  #1290 (`\FUNC(...)` not spreading over a returned LIST)
    was measured to be a DIFFERENT mechanism â the refgen operand's context
    annotation, not the deref â and was NOT taken here.

(2) `$#{'main::ga'}` â **SHIPPED** (c4434fa7).  A CL string IS a vector, so
    `p-array-last-index`'s vectorp arm answered the NAME's length; both the
    read and the write now go through %p-symref-array.  Rows 237-refs and
    238-refs left known-fail.tsv.

(3) `utf8::is_utf8` â **RULED DIVERGENCE, filed as #1389** (40050d95).  15
    shapes measured; both cheaper rules fail (see #1389).  Row 243-string
    re-pointed at #1389; docs/not-supported.md carries the ruling.

(4) `eval @array` â **SHIPPED** (03623f62).  eval's operand is an EXPR in
    SCALAR context; p-scalar is the one coercion.  295-string-eval left
    known-fail.tsv; perl-tests/eval.t 129 -> 131.

(5) `exists $string->{k}` â **NOT A SINGLETON, filed as #1390** (317ee066).
    NINE spellings diverge together under `use strict`, and the cause is the
    ruled "`use strict 'refs'` is not enforced".  Row 253-string re-pointed.

(6) a sort-of-literals alias â **SIZED AND FILED as #1391** (94adc02c).  Not
    "one flag on literal boxes": 18 shapes, per ELEMENT, propagating through
    sort/reverse/grep and not map, and a literal in a foreach list is a RAW
    value with no box to flag.  Row 272-sort re-pointed.

(7) a trailing BAREWORD statement â **SHIPPED** (f377a678).  #266's
    three-valued asymmetry at a new site, plus two guards the measurement
    forced (the emitter's builtin table for `study;`/`reset;`, and rewriting
    IN the lowered form so the context wraps survive).  Rows 213-oo and
    239-refs left known-fail.tsv.

(8) the `:utf8` pipe (258-io) â **NOT IN THIS BRIEF** and untouched.  It is
    the only #1249 corpus row left; the task stays OPEN for it.

CORPUS: ir-conform 316 pass / 0 fail / 29 known / 0 stale (from 287/58 when
the corpus was written; 311/34 at this batch's start).


=== ITEM (4) CORRECTED (s473h, after Fable review) ===
The first fix coerced the operand VALUE with p-scalar; perl imposes scalar
CONTEXT, so a CALL in that slot runs with wantarray FALSE.  `eval`/`evalbytes`
now join the scalar-argument named-unary family in PExpr::child_context (the
operand is emitted `(p-scalar-ctx â¦)`); the runtime p-scalar stays as the
second half, because p-scalar-ctx of a bare array read yields the vector and
`eval @a` IS its count.  `eval BLOCK` is a different node (p-eval-block) and
keeps the caller context.  The guard row Fable asked for turned up #1393
(a named-unary builtin given a parenthesised list got N arguments instead of
one comma expression -- `eval (1,2,3)` CRASHED), fixed in the same commit.
Eight probe shapes identical to perl 5.40.3; guards Pl/t/eval-01.t 51 -> 57.
